chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I heard him saying: It is recommended for the sick person that he give to the beggar with his own hand, and that he instruct the beggar to supplicate for him.

key_terms.السَّائِل: The beggar, the one who asks; refers broadly to any person seeking charity
key_terms.يَدْعُوَ: To supplicate, make du'a; the invocation of the beggar on behalf of the sick person
key_terms.يُسْتَحَبُّ: Mustahabb — a recommended (non-obligatory) act that earns reward if performed

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about a sick person giving charity?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that it is a recommended (mustahabb) act for a sick person to personally hand charity to a beggar rather than delegating it, and to then ask the beggar to pray on their behalf. This combines the spiritual merit of direct charitable giving with seeking intercession through the prayers of the poor, who are considered especially close to divine mercy. The practice reflects the Islamic understanding that personal engagement in charity and the supplication of the needy carry particular blessing for the giver.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘
I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘It is recommended for the sick one that he should give the beggar with his own hands, and he should instruct the beggar that he supplicates for him’.
en.sarwar: 9. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
it is preferable for a person suffering from illness to give charity with his own hand to one who asks for charity, then ask him to pray for him.”
